title: How much does a trip to Japan from the US cost? A full budget breakdown
summary: See how much a trip to Japan costs from the US, Europe, Africa, South America and North America, with flight, hotel and daily budgets. Compare.
body_markdown:
You pull up flights to Tokyo. $1,200 round trip from New York. You check hotels. $150 a night in Shinjuku. You start doing the maths and the number climbs past $3,000 before you've added food or a single bullet train ticket. Then you land and discover that a bowl of tonkotsu ramen costs $7, a metro ride across Tokyo is $2, and a Shinto shrine charges $3 to enter. The flights and hotels are expensive. Everything else is cheaper than a week in most European or American cities.


A one-week trip to Japan costs roughly $1,500 to $4,000 per person, depending on where you fly from and your travel style. Budget travellers can manage around $1,500 to $2,200, mid-range around $2,500 to $4,000, and luxury $6,000 or more. Flights are the biggest variable by region.


This guide breaks down costs from five origin regions so you can budget accurately regardless of where you're flying from. For help building your itinerary, use the[free trip itinerary template](https://grey.co/blog/trip-itinerary-template) .


## **How much does a trip to Japan cost? Budget range overview**


How much is a trip to Japan? The answer depends on three things: where you fly from, how you sleep, and how fast you move between cities. Here's the range for a solo traveller spending 7 nights:


Travel Style 7-Night Total (Solo) Daily Spend (Excl. Flight)


Budget (hostels, konbini meals, local trains) $1,500 to $2,200 $80 to $120


Mid-range (business hotels, restaurants, JR Pass) $2,500 to $4,000 $150 to $250


Luxury (ryokans, kaiseki, taxis) $5,000 to $8,000+ $400 to $700+


‍


The highest single cost is always the flight. After that, accommodation and intercity transport (especially bullet trains) determine which tier you're in. Food, attractions, and local transport are comparatively cheap. A budget traveller eating at convenience stores, taking local trains, and sleeping in hostels can see most of what Japan offers for under $100 a day.


## **How much does a trip to Japan cost from the USA?**


Round-trip flights from major US cities to Tokyo (Narita or Haneda) typically cost $800 to $1,400 in economy. Direct flights from the West Coast (LA, San Francisco, Seattle) are cheaper and shorter (10 to 11 hours). East Coast departures (New York, Chicago) are more expensive and add connection time or a longer direct route (13 to 14 hours).


Low season (January to early March, excluding holidays) drops fares to the $700 to $900 range. Cherry blossom season (late March to mid-April) and Golden Week (late April to early May) push fares past $1,200. Summer (July to August) and autumn foliage (October to November) sit in the middle.


Expense Budget Mid-Range


Round-trip flight $700 to $1,000 $1,000 to $1,400


Accommodation (7 nights) $280 to $490 $560 to $1,050


Food (7 days) $175 to $280 $280 to $490


Transport (7 days) $100 to $180 $250 to $400


Activities (7 days) $50 to $100 $100 to $250


Total per person $1,500 to $2,200 $2,500 to $4,000

## **How much does a trip to Japan cost from North America (Canada and Mexico)?**


From Canada, round-trip flights from Vancouver are the cheapest, ranging from $800 to $1,200 (direct flights available). Toronto adds $200 to $400 to those ranges because most routes connect through Vancouver, Seattle, or a Pacific hub. From Mexico City, flights typically route through the US or via a transpacific airline and cost $1,000 to $1,700.


Once in Japan, daily costs are identical to those for US travellers. The only difference is the flight. Budget total for 7 nights from Canada: $1,600 to $2,400. From Mexico: $1,800 to $2,800.


## **How much does a trip to Japan cost from Europe?**


Flights from London, Paris, and Frankfurt to Tokyo run $700 to $1,300 (roughly EUR 650 to EUR 1,200). Airlines like Finnair (via Helsinki), Turkish Airlines (via Istanbul), and ANA (direct from London or Paris) compete on this route, keeping prices reasonable despite the distance. Low-season fares dip below $700.


The yen's weakness against the euro and pound in recent years has made Japan's daily costs cheaper for European travellers than they look in dollar terms. A meal that costs 1,500 yen ($10) feels like a bargain against London or Paris restaurant prices. Budget total for 7 nights from Europe: $1,500 to $2,200. Mid-range: $2,300 to $3,800.


## **How much does a trip to japan cost from Africa?**


There are no direct flights from any African city to Japan. The most common routes connect through Dubai (Emirates), Doha (Qatar Airways), or Istanbul (Turkish Airlines). From Lagos, Nairobi, or Johannesburg, round-trip fares range from $900 to $1,800, depending on the season and layover time. Two-stop itineraries are cheaper but add 20+ hours of travel.


Once in Japan, costs are the same as for any other origin. The flight premium is the main budget difference. Budget total for 7 nights from Africa: $1,700 to $2,600. Mid-range: $2,700 to $4,200. Currency conversion is a factor: if you're earning in naira, rand, or shillings, holding USD or yen before travel avoids unfavourable airport exchange rates.


## **How much does a trip to Japan cost from South America?**


Flights from Sao Paulo or Buenos Aires to Tokyo are among the longest and most expensive: $1,300 to $2,200 round trip. Most routes connect through the US (Dallas, Houston, LA) or the Middle East. Timing matters: January and February fares are lowest. No direct flights exist from South America to Japan as of 2026.


Budget total for 7 nights from South America: $2,000 to $3,000. Mid-range: $3,000 to $4,500. The flight is the single largest expense. Once on the ground, Japan's daily costs are manageable, but the airfare takes a bigger bite of the total budget than from any other region.


## **Trip to Japan cost breakdown: Flights, hotels, food and activities**


Here's every line item for a 7-day Japan trip, regardless of origin:


Expense Budget Range Notes


Round-trip flight (US origin) $700 to $1,400 West Coast cheaper; book 2 to 3 months ahead


Accommodation per night $40 to $200 Hostels $40 to $70, business hotels $80 to $150, ryokans $150 to $400+


JR Pass (7-day) $335 Covers bullet trains; only worth it if you take 3+ long-distance trips


Local transport per day $5 to $15 Metro, buses; buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card


Food per day $25 to $70 Konbini breakfast $3 to $5, ramen $7 to $12, sit-down dinner $15 to $40


Activities per day $10 to $35 Temples $3 to $5, museums $7 to $15, theme parks $55 to $75


eSIM data (7 days) $4 to $10 Prepaid data plan; essential for maps and translation


Travel insurance (7 days) $15 to $50 Basic medical + trip cancellation coverage


‍


**On the JR Pass:** at $335 for 7 days, the Japan Rail Pass is only worth buying if you plan at least 2 to 3 long-distance bullet train trips (Tokyo to Kyoto is $100 each way). If you're staying in one city, local trains and metro passes are much cheaper. If you're buying JR tickets individually, hold Japanese yen in advance and pay at station kiosks to avoid airport exchange markups.


**How to Budget and Pay for Your Trip to Japan**


Japan is still heavily cash-dependent in smaller shops, izakayas, and rural areas. Major chains and department stores accept cards, but you'll need cash for temple admission, street food, local buses, and smaller restaurants. Here's how to handle the money side:


**Carry some yen in cash.** Withdraw from 7-Eleven ATMs (available nationwide, 24/7) or exchange before departure. Airport exchange desks give the worst rates.


**Use a card with no foreign transaction fee.** Japan's card acceptance has improved, but foreign transaction fees of 1.5 to 3% eat into your budget on every tap.[Grey's virtual card](http://grey.co/cards) charges a 1% conversion fee capped at $6. ## **Frequently asked questions about the cost of a trip to Japan from the US**


### **How much does a trip to Japan cost for 7 days?**


A 7-day trip to Japan costs $1,500 to $4,000 per person from the US, depending on travel style. Budget travellers staying in hostels and eating at convenience stores spend $1,500 to $2,200. Mid-range travellers using business hotels, JR Pass, and restaurants spend $2,500 to $4,000. Flights are the biggest variable: West Coast departures are $200 to $400 cheaper than East Coast.


### **Is Japan expensive for tourists?**


Japan's reputation for being expensive is outdated. Daily spending (food, transport, activities) is lower than in London, Paris, or New York. A bowl of ramen costs $7 to $12. A metro ride is $2 to $4. Temple admission is $3 to $5. The expensive parts are flights (especially from Africa and South America) and bullet trains ($100+ per trip). The weak yen has also made Japan cheaper for visitors holding dollars, euros, or pounds.


### **How much spending money do I need per day in Japan?**


Budget travellers need $80 to $120 per day for accommodation, food, transport, and activities. Mid-range travellers need $150 to $250 per day. This excludes flights. Carry some cash (yen) for smaller shops and rural areas. Use a card with no foreign transaction fee for larger purchases to avoid 1.5 to 3% markups on every tap.


### **Is the JR Pass worth it?**


Only if you take 3 or more long-distance bullet train trips in 7 days. At $335, the JR Pass breaks even if you ride from Tokyo to Kyoto round-trip ($200) plus one more Shinkansen trip. If you're staying in one city or only making one intercity trip, buying individual tickets is cheaper. The JR Pass also covers some local JR lines, which adds value if you're moving between cities daily.


### **What is the cheapest month to visit Japan?**


January and February are the cheapest months. Flights drop to $700 to $900 from the US, and hotels offer low-season rates. The weather is cold but dry. Avoid the last week of December (New Year) and the first week of January (holiday crowds). Late May (after Golden Week) and September are also good values with better weather.


### **How much would a trip to Japan cost from Africa?**


A 7-day trip to Japan from Lagos, Nairobi, or Johannesburg costs $1,700 to $4,200, depending on travel style. Flights are the biggest expense: $900 to $1,800 round trip via Dubai, Doha, or Istanbul. Daily costs in Japan are the same regardless of origin. Consider holding USD or yen before departure to avoid poor exchange rates at African airports.
